text:
Maria (CS): Jonah from Rivermark just flagged a big regression on embeddings p95/p99 after yesterday's catalog refresh. their dashboard shows p95 up from ~120ms to ~820ms for /v1/embeddings over last 3 hours. they say it's blocking nightly analytics jobs.

Jonah (Rivermark): confirmed — jobs that used to finish in 10m now 50-70m. not seeing big request rate changes on our side, same batch sizes.

Maria (CS): adding SRE / platform. @Kevin (SRE) any immediate ideas?

Kevin (SRE): looking. first pass — can you paste the tenant id and a sample request id? also which model routing (open-embedding-1 / rdl-small)?

Jonah (Rivermark): tenant=rv_mark_42, sample request id= req_20260314_kk5h, model=open-embed-v2

Nora (SupportEng): pulling logs. I see a cluster of slow tails on nodes in us-west-2a around 03:10-04:00 UTC. p99 correlates with high GPU memory spikes on host gpu-node-17.

Eve (Observability): throwing up a quick grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/embeds/rv_mark_42?from=now-6h — you can see p95 jump and host metric overlays.

Kevin (SRE): running a fast query against request traces. snippet: 
``` 
SELECT request_id, duration_ms, host FROM traces WHERE tenant='rv_mark_42' AND ts > now()-6h ORDER BY ts;
``` 
Most slow requests show `host=gpu-node-17` and `duration_ms` 600-1200ms.

Kevin (SRE): checking host metrics: `nvidia_smi` shows 98% GPU util, but only ~30% runned by open-embed-v2 processes. other PIDs belong to `batch-encoder` jobs from tenant `rv_mark_99` (internal partner). looks like noisy neighbor memory+cuda-scheduling pressure causing kernel preemption and big latency tails.

Lee (Platform): is rv_mark_99 doing large batched matrix ops? we had a canary earlier that launched a heavy async bulk-encode task.

infra-bot: deploy_event: canary bulk-encode-job v1.2 triggered in us-west-2a at 2026-03-14T02:58:04Z.

Nora (SupportEng): immediate mitigation options: 1) per-tenant throttling for rv_mark_99 on that node pool, 2) migrate affected tenants (rv_mark_42) to a different pool/dedicated capacity, 3) apply node-level cgroup/GPU isolation where supported.

Maria (CS): customer asks for fastest fix that doesn't require code changes on their side. which is quickest?

Kevin (SRE): quickest is to route rv_mark_42 requests to a different AZ/pool that doesn't have the noisy job. I can temporarily add a per-tenant routing rule to prefer us-west-2b. doing that now (will need ~2-3 mins to propagate).

Kevin (SRE): `route set --tenant rv_mark_42 --prefer-pool us-west-2b --reason "mitigate noisy neighbor"` -> applied.

Eve (Observability): metrics after routing: p95 for rv_mark_42 down to ~140ms within 90s. p99 still slightly elevated (~220ms) due to some in-flight requests.

Jonah (Rivermark): thanks — performance looks back to normal on our side. any ETA on a permanent fix?

Lee (Platform): follow-ups: we're going to 1) add a per-tenant throttle policy for heavy background encoders (rv_mark_99) to cap concurrent GPU batches, 2) add a bespoke allowlist for large async jobs so they land on dedicated capacity rather than shared pools, 3) add auto-detection: if p99 exceeds threshold and node-level cross-tenant GPU memory > 80%, then proactively migrate affected tenants.

Kevin (SRE): I'm opening an internal escalation ticket and scheduling a quick maintenance window to migrate the bulk-encode canary off shared pool. ticket: INC-2026-324.

Nora (SupportEng): also added a short-term per-tenant throttle rule for rv_mark_99: `throttle set --tenant rv_mark_99 --max-concurrency 4 --window 60s --reason "noisy-neighbor mitigation"`. That will prevent huge background spikes while we sort dedicated placement.

Maria (CS): told Jonah we'll keep them posted and offered to move them to a Dedicated pool if they want stricter isolation (note: commercial conversation).

Jonah (Rivermark): appreciate the swift response — keep us updated. would also like an export of slow traces for our internal logs.

Kevin (SRE): export prepared: s3://redwood-support/rv_mark_42/exports/2026-03-14/slow-traces-req_20260314_kk5h.json.gz. shared with Jonah.

Eve (Observability): added a new alert rule: `tenant.p99 > 500ms for 5m` -> pager to eng-oncall and CS channel. also instrumentation improved to include GPU-scheduler-wait metric in traces.

Lee (Platform): long term: we will add workload classification (embedding-async vs realtime) so heavy async jobs can be opt-in to a 'bulk' pool. ops doc: https://wiki.redwood.internal/platform/bulk-pools.

Maria (CS): closing action items for CS: confirm customer sees stable p95 next 24h, follow-up on dedicated capacity upsell if needed.

Nora (SupportEng): leaving this thread open; will update when the bulk canary is redeployed to dedicated pool.

infra-bot: deploy_event: bulk-encode-job v1.2 relocated to dedicated-pool-bulk-01 at 2026-03-14T05:02:11Z.

Eve (Observability): final check: rv_mark_42 p95 stayed <170ms for the last 4 hours. marking incident mitigated.

Kevin (SRE): root cause: noisy neighbor GPU memory/cuda-scheduling pressure from bulk async encoder on shared pool. mitigations: per-tenant throttles, routing policy change, dedicated pool relocation, alerting + instrumentation.

Maria (CS): thanks team — Jonah we'll circle back with a short RCA doc and the export link. :thumbsup:

Jonah (Rivermark): thanks everyone :)
